label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. They form a psychologically resilient cluster characterized by minimal mental health distress across all three measured dimensions, with anxiety scores near floor level and depression and loneliness scores well below typical thresholds of concern.
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily screen/internet use
behavior_markers: Very low loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.72), indicating strong social connectedness
Minimal depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.30), well below clinical screening thresholds
Near-zero anxiety symptoms (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.03), suggesting very low psychological distress
Moderate and controlled screen/internet use (1–3 hours daily)
Higher educational attainment suggesting structured daily routines and goal orientation

label: Digitally Immersed & Emotionally Distressed
summary: This profile represents highly educated women who spend more than 5 hours daily online and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Their UCLA-8 loneliness score (1.72), PHQ-9 depression score (1.73), and GAD-7 anxiety score (2.15) are all in the higher range, suggesting a pattern of co-occurring psychological distress. With 180 respondents in this cluster, it represents a substantial subgroup where heavy digital engagement coincides with notable emotional vulnerability across all three measured dimensions.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, daily screen/internet use exceeding 5 hours
behavior_markers: Reports elevated loneliness despite presumably high digital connectivity
Displays the highest anxiety levels among profiles (GAD-7 mean ~2.15)
Engages in prolonged daily screen time (more than 5 hours)
Demonstrates co-occurrence of loneliness, depression, and anxiety rather than isolated symptoms
tone: Concerned and empathetic, highlighting the convergence of heavy digital use and multi-dimensional psychological distress in an educated female population
